stage0Implications: The handwritten manifest produced both a 1280x720 landscape composition and an exact-ratio 1080x1920 center crop. Trim, concat, scale, neutral subtitle burn-in, and audio gain were exercised without a shell command or source overwrite.
All four outputs contained H.264 Main video and AAC 48 kHz stereo audio and completed full decode. Landscape A/V end difference was 0.023367 seconds and vertical was 0.014633 seconds.
Two iterations of each composition were byte-identical and decoded-stream-identical on this machine in one session. Cross-machine, cross-GPU, and driver-change reproducibility were not measured.

Four output samples were reverse-mapped through observed output PTS, the handwritten segment map, and observed source PTS. The maximum source-frame selection error was 0.014166667 seconds, below the previously observed 0.635-second maximum source frame duration.

Every mapped frame was closer in grayscale MAD to its expected transformed source frame than to a source frame five seconds away. This demonstrates content correspondence for four samples, not perceptual quality or universal mapping accuracy.

The neutral ASS active-frame difference exceeded the inactive control, and the half-amplitude audio control measured -6.1 dB versus -6.0206 dB expected. These are mechanism controls with unapproved Stage 0 tolerances.
The subtitle is not source-transcript-derived, so subtitle-to-source-speech and content-level OriginRef traceability remain unmeasured for later implementation tasks.

assessment.interpretation: ST-012 demonstrates the required local render mechanisms and piecewise output-to-source time lookup on two short handwritten compositions. It does not approve visual quality, audio delivery targets, subtitle content traceability, or production tolerances.
measurementCorrections: The initial planning sketch used a 1280x2160 crop, which is not 9:16. The executed manifest uses an exact 1080x1920 centered crop at x=1380, y=120.
The first implementation concatenated all video labels before all audio labels. FFmpeg concat requires per-segment interleaving, so the executed graph uses [v0][a0][v1][a1].

The first formal run expected a rounded whole-composition frame count of 300. Because fps is applied independently to each five-second segment, the executed landscape graph emits floor(5*30000/1001) twice, or 298 frames; the validator now derives the expectation per segment.
Adversarial review added same-machine/GPU/driver reproducibility scope and explicit flags that neutral subtitle rendering does not establish source-speech or content-level OriginRef traceability.
openQuestions: Human visual review and a production visual-quality threshold are not available; four MAD controls are mechanism evidence only.
The 1 dB audio-gain tolerance is a Stage 0 control parameter, not a delivery loudness requirement.
Cross-machine, cross-driver, CPU/Media Foundation fallback, and longer-composition reproducibility remain unmeasured.
Subtitle content traceability, safe-zone/layout quality, and output-to-source mapping for all future edit operation types remain later implementation and acceptance work.
Fixture rights remain unconfirmed, so rendered files stay in ignored local evidence and cannot be externally published.
Final render profile adoption and thresholds require ST-015 human approval.
assessment.privacy: Source-derived videos, PTS files, frames, and audio remain in an ignored local directory protected by a non-inheriting three-principal ACL. The canonical contains only hashes, dimensions, codec data, timing, aggregate pixel/audio measurements, and bounded interpretations; no source pixels, audio samples, transcript, absolute path, or command arguments are included.
